name: TX-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+24 district lean makes a Democratic win historically improbable
Moran has raised about $2.4M versus roughly $20K for Prince, with under $1,500 cash on hand for the challenger
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 97% to win
No polls or expert ratings signal any competitiveness
model.rationale: The district's R+24 lean, Moran's roughly hundred-to-one fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 97% Republican leave the Democratic challenger without a visible path, so the forecast holds a wide Republican margin.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or a dramatic shift in the national environment could put this seat in play, and no such evidence exists.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-01 covers deep East Texas, a district that has voted Republican by roughly 24 points in recent elections. Representative Nathaniel Moran is seeking reelection with a substantial financial edge, having raised about $2.4 million and holding nearly $1 million on hand. Democratic nominee Yolanda Prince has raised about $20,000 and reports under $1,500 in the bank, leaving little visible campaign infrastructure.

No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets put the Republican's chances near 97%. The combination of a heavily Republican electorate, an incumbent with a large money advantage, and a minimally funded challenger makes this one of the least competitive House races on the map. Barring an unforeseen development, Moran is positioned to win by a wide margin in November.
